label: Flood / surface water (monthly, Sentinel-1 SAR) — trend 2018→year (Sen's slope)
scale: linear, symmetric about 0 (fixed across years: 98th percentile of |slope|)
native_resolution: 10 m Sentinel-1 RTC read at 160 m, classified on a 0.004 deg (~440 m) grid
source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 IW GRD RTC (sentinel-1-rtc) via Microsoft Planetary Computer
basis: wet-season (Jun-Sep) mean water/flooded fraction (%) of each 0.02° cell from the monthly Sentinel-1 classification (gap-filled as in flood_s1_pipeline). Missing months are filled by the climatology-anomaly method (yearly = mean monthly climatology + mean anomaly of the observed months); a year needs >= half of the season observed unless stated otherwise.
notes: Each image = per-pixel Theil-Sen (Sen's) slope of the yearly values from 2018 through the image year (>= 3 years), in percentage points/yr. brown = drier / less water, teal = wetter / more water; white = no change. No significance test is applied per pixel: with 3-8 yearly points a slope is a description of change, not proof of a trend.
